title: Why Being in the Market Beats Timing the Market Every Time
summary: Historically, staying invested has done better than jumping in and out, because the best days tend to land right next to the worst ones.
body_markdown:
## How Astor helps with the urge to react


A lot of the pressure to time the market comes from headlines that have nothing to do with what you own.


Astor is a personal investing agent on iPhone and in iMessage. It connects to the brokerage, retirement and crypto accounts you already have at most major US institutions through Plaid, learns what you own, and follows every position along with the earnings dates, filings and headlines that touch them. When nothing matters to your portfolio, it stays quiet. When something crosses a line you care about, it texts you right away with what happened, why it matters to you, and what you could do, with the reasoning and sources behind it.


That changes what a bad news day looks like. Instead of reading every scary headline and wondering whether it applies to you, you hear about the ones that touch your holdings, with an explanation, and you decide whether anything needs doing.[At a glance](https://www.astor.app/blog/at-a-glance) adds a five-second daily check with two lines on what moved your money today and why, so a red number comes with a reason.


Astor doesn’t trade, rebalance or move money in your connected accounts, and it doesn’t run a managed portfolio. You make every decision, and since the AI can be wrong, it shows its sources. Astor is free to start and available in the US only. You can[see how it works](https://www.astor.app/#how-it-works) , or read[how to actually review your investment portfolio](https://www.astor.app/blog/how-to-actually-review-your-investment-portfolio) .
